correctness.rationale: Direct literal read counts yield y_j=x_j+x_(j+1), and all collisions lie on the alternating integer kernel. Fixed sum kills this kernel for odd n. Even-n nonnegative translates have a unique odd-minimum-zero representative; exact stars-and-bars subtraction yields T_s and H_s, including n=2 and k=0. Explicit representatives reach the worst fiber. The included separate literal-read enumerator matches every formula for 63 (n,k) pairs, 19,440 source multisets. Finite tests do not replace the complete proof.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text comparisons with the motivating 2021 pooled substring-profile paper, its 2022 generalized version, related 2023 multi-string random/noisy models, 2024 constant-weight all-length composition reconstruction and 2018 single-strand multispectra distinguish the exact claim from the published asymptotic, compositional, or single-source results. Multiple actual equivalent/stronger-table searches found no covering theorem; risk of an unindexed path-incidence equivalent remains.
residual_risks: An exact enumeration for nonnegative integer path-incidence fibers may already exist under algebraic statistics or graph-theory terminology and be indexed outside string-reconstruction literature.

The accessible Yang–Chen 2024 constant-weight compositional characterization was inspected in relevant sections rather than formally reduced for every special parameter; its observation is different and its results are not currently known to imply the literal fixed-length fiber census.

value.rationale: The maximal proper read length is a canonical reconstruction boundary and one-marker strands are the natural extreme sparse-message regime. The theorem supplies an all-length exact parity threshold, the full ambiguity-fiber size distribution, a tight worst-case inverse-list bound, and a closed-form largest zero-error reconstruction code—not an arbitrary finite slice or routine table recomputation. It quantifies polynomial-degree information loss from pooling nearly complete reads.
